ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a quadrilateral broken-line path composed of four blue line segments, and an exterior angle is marked at each vertex, respectively 139° on the left side, 6x° at the top, 9x° at the lower right, and 2x° slightly left of the bottom. Reasoning: According to the theorem on the sum of exterior angles of a polygon, when one exterior angle is taken at each vertex of a polygon, the sum of the exterior angles is 360°. Therefore 139 + 6x + 9x + 2x = 360. Combining like terms gives 139 + 17x = 360, so 17x = 221, and solving gives x = 13.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a four-sided polygonal path with one exterior angle marked at each vertex: 139°, 6x°, 9x°, and 2x°. Use the exterior-angle sum theorem for a polygon: the sum of one exterior angle at each vertex is 360°. Set up 139 + 6x + 9x + 2x = 360, so 17x = 221 and x = 13.
